title: Blood Glucose Trending on Insulin Drip
scenario: A 54-year-old client in diabetic ketoacidosis is on a continuous regular insulin infusion titrated to hourly point-of-care glucose readings.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: The glucose has fallen to 182 mg/dL. According to standard DKA protocol, what should the nurse anticipate next?

options.text: Adding dextrose to the IV fluids to prevent hypoglycemia while the insulin drip continues
Giving a rapid IV bolus of regular insulin

questions.rationale: When glucose approaches roughly 200 mg/dL in DKA, dextrose is added so the insulin infusion can continue to clear ketones without causing hypoglycemia; the drip is not stopped until the anion gap closes.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Which additional trend on the flowsheet most requires the nurse's attention?

options.text: The steadily falling potassium, now 3.4 mEq/L

questions.rationale: Insulin drives potassium intracellularly, so potassium falls during DKA treatment; the downward trend to 3.4 mEq/L signals a need for replacement before dangerous hypokalemia develops.
